summary: ACCEPT after five rounds. All four round-4 blockers fixed, verified by EXECUTION and by 7/7 mutants killed, each target confirmed to occur exactly once before mutating so none was a no-op. N1: the filled-intent CTE now filters only intent_type='open' - ti.status='filled' is deleted, so every open intent holding a real BUY fill is counted. ⭐ The test that DEFENDED the bug is INVERTED, not removed: it now asserts "ti.status='filled'" NOT in the CTE, on the live SQL, plus a new partial-fill-then-cancelled control. Mutant (i) re-adding the filter reproduces the exact production defect I measured - the filled DDD vanishes, first-rate prints 50.0 instead of 75.0, and it is published as a GRADEABLE no-entry cross. N1b: the tautological RECONCILED verdict is deleted repo-wide; the file now prints a line ONLY on disagreement, so no vacuous pass is published. N2: no_entry_gradeable now requires slot_gradeable and the log verdict; the test that required the old behaviour was rewritten rather than deleted. N3: any ambiguous round trip downgrades, and ambiguous=/invalid_price= appear on both the per-account and VERDICT lines. N4: the five-state historical_log_verdict from the sibling script is implemented against the REAL reader and gates both the first-rate and no-entry sections, so a rotated log is no longer byte-identical to a quiet day. No remaining number in the file publishes a false zero. NON-BLOCKING, all failing SAFE toward COULD_NOT_TELL: (1) trips_verdict collapses to COULD_NOT_TELL whenever accounts mix GRADEABLE with UNEXERCISED - since ORB is decommissioned that is the NORMAL daily shape, so the machine-readable aggregate is a permanently dead signal; an UNEXERCISED account should not veto. (2) A real zero-entry day cannot be graded, because slot_gradeable requires total_entries>0 and no_entry now depends on it - yet 'we armed 5 times and entered nothing' is the most actionable EOD result there is; add a populations_consistent AND total_entries==0 branch. (3) The no-entry detail list truncates at 10 with no 'N more' marker - the count above reconciles so it is detectable, but it is the head -N shape. (4) MEDIAN prints on the line after a COULD_NOT_TELL account verdict, so a copied median loses its verdict; embed it as format_first_slot_rate does. (5) _historical_log_verdict returns an UNVALIDATED getattr string, so a future check.py attribute of that name would override the verdict - validate against the five known states.
